info.name: nango-events
info.description: Metering API. Ingest single events or batches (queued, 202), see them rejected when invalid, and query them raw or aggregated per time bucket. Events carry optional metadata for billing. Timestamps and query ranges are computed per request (collection pre-request script) so the queries always cover today. Set `baseUrl` if the API is not on localhost:3000; `accountId` must be a seeded account.

exec: pm.test("six event types, each with a unit and required metadata", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d).to.have.lengthOf(6); d.forEach(t => pm.expect(t).to.have.keys("name", "description", "unit", "metadata")); });

request.description: What can be metered, the billable unit for each event, and the metadata fields it must carry.

item.name: Ingest
item.description: POST /ingest: one event. Answers 202 once the event is on the queue; the consumer writes it to Postgres a moment later.

exec: pm.test("queued with the metadata", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.eventName).to.eql("connection_created"); pm.expect(d.metadata.connection_id).to.eql("conn_42"); });
pm.test("metadata kept as sent", () => { const m = pm.response.json().data.metadata; pm.expect(m.records).to.eql(250); pm.expect(m.model).to.eql("Contact"); });

request.description: event_id is the idempotency key: send the same one twice and the event is stored once (the second POST still answers 202). Omit it and the API generates a UUID.
Send this twice quickly (or run it with 2 iterations): both answer 202, but GET /events shows the event once. The consumer skips the second insert because account + event_id is unique.

item.name: Batch
item.description: POST /ingest/batch: up to 100 events in one request, each with a required timestamp. Valid events are queued; the response says how many (`success`) and lists every event that was not, with its index and why (`errors`). Limits: 10 batches per account per minute, and every event also counts against the account + event name limit shared with single ingest (100/min).

exec: pm.test("3 success, 0 failed", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data).to.eql({ success: 3, failed: 0, errors: [] }));

request.description: Counts once against each account's batch allowance.

25 events of each of four kinds. Every event counts against its account + event limit (100/min), the same counter as single ingest, so this can run up to four times a minute before events start being rejected.

item.name: Batch with some valid and some failing events (partial success)

exec: pm.test("2 success, 3 failed", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.success).to.eql(2); pm.expect(d.failed).to.eql(3); });

pm.test("each failure names the event index and the reason", () => { const e = pm.response.json().data.errors; pm.expect(e.map(x => [x.index, x.reason])).to.eql([[1, "invalid"], [3, "invalid"], [4, "unknown_account"]]); });

request.description: Events 0 and 2 are queued. Event 1 has an unknown event name, event 3 is missing its timestamp, event 4 belongs to an unknown account: all three come back in errors with their index and reason.

exec: pm.test("names the field and the allowed values", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.include("event_name: Invalid option"));
pm.test("every bad field is listed", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().details.map(d => d.path)).to.eql(["account_id", "metadata", "timestamp"]));
pm.test("account not found", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql("Account acc_unknown not found"));

request.description: Only seeded accounts are accepted. Checked before the rate limiter, so unknown ids never use quota.

item.name: Metadata missing a required field (per the event catalogue)

exec: pm.test("names the missing and wrong metadata fields", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().details.map(d => d.path)).to.eql(["metadata.model", "metadata.records"]));

request.description: records_synced must carry connection_id, model and records (an integer). See GET /event-types for every event's required fields.

item.name: Query
item.description: GET /events. Raw events newest first, or with `window` one count per time bucket.

exec: pm.test("returns the events ingested above, newest first", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data.length).to.be.at.least(1); pm.expect(b.meta).to.have.keys("total", "limit", "offset"); });

pm.test("only connection_created, at least one", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.length).to.be.at.least(1); d.forEach(e => pm.expect(e.eventName).to.eql("connection_created")); });

pm.test("today's events, all inside the range", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.length).to.be.at.least(1); d.forEach(e => { pm.expect(new Date(e.timestamp)).to.be.at.least(new Date(pm.variables.get("todayStart"))); pm.expect(new Date(e.timestamp)).to.be.at.most(new Date(pm.variables.get("todayEnd"))); }); });

request.description: from/to are today's UTC midnight to tomorrow's, computed per request.

exec: pm.test("24 hourly buckets for today, at least one non-empty", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.windowSeconds).to.eql(3600); pm.expect(b.meta.total).to.eql(24); pm.expect(b.buckets.some(x => x.count > 0)).to.be.true; });

request.description: window = bucket size (minute, hour, day, or 15m, 6h, 1w). Buckets align to the clock; a 24h range at 1h is exactly 24 values.

item.name: Rate limit
item.description: Used in the demo to trigger 429s and the Slack alert. Run with the Collection Runner.

exec: pm.test("202 for the first 100 in a minute, then 429", () => pm.expect([202, 429]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: 100 per minute per account + event. Uses its own account so it never blocks the other requests.

exec: pm.test("202 for the first 10 batches in a minute, then 429 with the event listed as rate_limited", () => { pm.expect([202, 429]).to.include(pm.response.code); if (pm.response.code === 429) pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.errors[0].reason).to.eql("rate_limited"); });

request.description: 10 batches per account per minute, separate from the single-ingest limit and with its own alert.
